answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before its claims can influence a shared reputation thread. A verifier selects claims at random and asks the agent to reproduce details from an earlier exchange; copied identities that mirror one another tend to fail when challenged on distinct histories. A failed check slashes the stake and lowers the reputation weight of linked claims. Sybil builders therefore must fund every identity separately and keep each one active long enough to earn trust, tying up capital at the ledge of every new claim.
